To: BST260 Teaching Team, Fall 2026




## Project Overview

For my BST260 final project, I plan to investigate two public health topics using datasets introduced in class. The project will consist of two separate analytical vignettes, focusing on hypertension risk factors in the NHANES dataset and patterns of waterborne disease outbreaks in the United States. I will use R for data exploration, visualization, and statistical analysis, and present the results through the finalproject R package and its pkgdown website.

## Analysis 1: NHANES

### Data Source

The first analysis will use data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), conducted by the National Center for Health Statistics at the CDC.

### Research Questions

I am interested in examining how BMI, age, and sex are associated with hypertension. Specifically, I plan to investigate whether hypertension prevalence differs across BMI categories and age groups, and whether the association between BMI and hypertension remains after accounting for age and sex.

### Proposed Methods

I will first examine the structure of the dataset, identify relevant variables, and summarize missing values. Descriptive statistics and visualizations will be used to explore distributions of BMI, age, and blood pressure measurements.

I plan to compare hypertension prevalence across demographic groups and use logistic regression to examine associations between hypertension and selected predictors, provided that an appropriate hypertension outcome can be constructed from the available variables. I will report effect estimates and uncertainty measures and consider the implications of the NHANES survey design.

### Limitations

Because NHANES is observational and cross sectional, the analysis cannot establish causal relationships. Missing data and potential confounding may also affect interpretation.

## Analysis 2: CDC Waterborne Illnesses

### Data Source

The second analysis will use the CDC waterborne illness dataset. I will document the original data source, coverage, variable definitions, and any relevant reporting limitations.

### Research Questions

I plan to examine how reported waterborne disease outbreaks vary over time and across geographic areas in the United States. I am particularly interested in identifying temporal trends, geographic differences, and patterns in outbreak characteristics where sufficient information is available.

### Proposed Methods

I will begin by inspecting the dataset and assessing data completeness. I will then calculate descriptive statistics for reported outbreaks and relevant characteristics.

Line plots will be used to visualize changes over time, while bar charts or geographic visualizations will be used to compare locations. Depending on the available variables, I may also explore differences across time periods or outbreak categories.

### Limitations

Reported outbreaks may not represent the true burden of waterborne disease because of underreporting, differences in surveillance practices, and incomplete records. Temporal or geographic differences will therefore be interpreted cautiously.

## Expected Deliverables

The final project will include a valid R package and a publicly accessible pkgdown website. I plan to develop two separate vignettes, one for each dataset. Each vignette will document data provenance, describe the variables and analytical objectives, present descriptive statistics and visualizations, and report findings with a discussion of uncertainty and limitations.

The overall goal is to produce a reproducible and clearly documented public health data analysis using the tools and methods introduced in BST260.
